edition.locus: Documenta Catholica Omnia Canones GR (sources/canones_GR.pdf), p. 2, Canon ι´

source_text: Τοὺς δὲ τὴν ἐντολὴν πληροῦντας, ἐκτὸς πάσης αἰσχροκερδείας πληροῦν δεῖ, μήτε μήνυτρα ἢ σῶστρα ἢ εὕρετρα ἢ ᾧ ὀνόματι ταῦτα καλοῦσιν ἀπαιτοῦντας.
thought_title: No reward for returning what was found
orientation: Those who return lost goods must not demand any reward for doing so.
pass_a_gloss: Those fulfilling the commandment must fulfil [it] apart from all shameful gain, not demanding informer's fees or salvage fees or finder's fees, or by whatever name they call these.

choices.english: a fee for information, for rescue, or for finding
choices.why: The three customary claims a finder might make; each named plainly.

pass_b_english: Those who fulfill the commandment must fulfill it free of all greed for shameful gain, without demanding a fee for information, for rescue, or for finding, or whatever name they give these.
notes: Rubric left out (editorial; it spells εὕρητρα, the text εὕρετρα; text kept). τὴν ἐντολήν = the command to return lost property set out in section 4 (Deuteronomy 22:1–3; Exodus 23:4); not cited again here because the canon names no text. αἰσχροκέρδεια rendered 'greed for shameful gain', matching section 2. μήνυτρα, σῶστρα, εὕρετρα = fees for information, for rescue (salvage), for finding.
drafter: claude (Claude Code, Opus); Cloudflare AI off

changes: spelling 'fulfil' → 'fulfill' to match the book's American spelling (Savior, neighbor in section 1)
